name: Michael Echols
current_role: Louisiana State Representative (District 14) and House Majority Leader
bio: Michael Echols has represented District 14 in the Louisiana House since 2020 and became House Republican Majority Leader in December 2025; he previously chaired the Monroe City Council. He works as a contractor and real estate developer and has served on the House Health and Welfare and Ways and Means committees. In 2024 he testified before a U.S. Senate committee about Steward Health Care's management of a Monroe-area hospital.

platform.point: Calls for enforcing immigration laws, returning people here illegally, and denaturalizing and deporting immigrants who defraud taxpayers.
Backs expanded domestic production, LNG exports, protection of Louisiana refineries and federal permitting reform.
Supports Trump's foreign policy, a stronger military, Israel's defense and confronting Iran.
Wants pricing transparency for pharmacy benefit managers and an end to their rebate practices.
Supports nationwide voter ID and the SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship to register for federal elections.
At a primary debate, suggested investing Social Security trust fund dollars in the market to address the shortfall.
Describes himself as pro-life and pledges to oppose federal restrictions on gun ownership.
Calls for aggressive audits of federal agencies and impeachment of federal judges who abuse their authority.

economy.evidence: Campaign pages call for reining in federal spending and removing regulations, and he received the NFIB small-business award for cutting regulatory burdens.

welfare.evidence: Proposes barring immigrants here illegally from benefits and suggested investing Social Security trust funds in the market, while pledging to protect Medicare benefits.

liberty.evidence: Averages a pro-life stance on abortion with a vote for 2024 permitless concealed carry (guns) and a 2022 bill barring job discrimination based on vaccination status.

security.evidence: Voted for 2024's HB2 giving police officers civil liability immunity and authored a 2023 resolution seeking weekly security threat reports from state agencies.

immigration.evidence: Campaign calls for returning people here illegally, denaturalizing and deporting immigrants who commit fraud, and ending benefits for those here illegally.

foreign.evidence: Campaign backs a stronger military, supporting Israel's defense against terrorism and confronting Iran.

energy.evidence: Campaigns on expanding domestic energy production and LNG exports, and at a debate called for ending federal tax credits for carbon capture.

education.evidence: Listed as a sponsor of 2024's HB745 creating the LA GATOR universal school choice program and voted for HB550 ending state approval of home study programs.

notes: Searched the campaign issues page, Wikipedia, legislative vote summaries and debate coverage; the LA GATOR sponsorship comes from a search summary of LegiScan, which blocked direct access. No clear statements found on tech regulation or religion in public life.

name: Stewart Cathey Jr.
bio: Stewart Cathey Jr. has served in the Louisiana Senate since 2020 and chairs its agriculture committee. He is a lieutenant colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve who deployed twice to Afghanistan as an engineer officer, and he runs a management consulting firm. He was born in Monroe and graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.

platform.point: Describes education as the foundation of a prosperous community.
Presents himself as an advocate for the district's farmers, ranchers and foresters.
Says voters want lower costs, secure borders, support for agriculture and a government that respects their values.
Campaign ads highlight his work on behalf of Louisiana veterans.
Authored a resolution asking Congress to require House candidates to live in the district they seek to represent.
Authored the 2022 Louisiana Consumer Fuel Choice Act barring local governments from restricting access to energy types.

liberty.evidence: Averages votes for 2024 permitless concealed carry and a 2023 bill for a Second Amendment sales tax holiday (guns) with a 2022 bill requiring drug testing of pregnant women at delivery (drugs).

security.evidence: Voted in 2024 for HB2 giving police officers civil liability immunity and authored a bill expanding detention authority for 17-year-olds.

immigration.evidence: General statement: lists secure borders among the district's priorities in his campaign launch.

energy.evidence: Authored the 2022 Consumer Fuel Choice Act, which bars local governments from limiting consumer access to fuels such as gasoline, diesel and natural gas.

notes: Searched the campaign site (home, about, news), launch coverage, Wikipedia and legislative bill and vote summaries; the campaign site has no issues page. No public positions found on the economy, welfare, foreign policy, tech, education policy or faith.

name: Pat Moore
bio: Patricia "Pat" Moore has represented District 17 in the Louisiana House since 2019 and is the Louisiana Democratic Party's endorsed candidate in the 5th District. She previously served on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury from 2007 to 2019 and retired from State Farm. She is from Monroe and graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.

platform.point: Aims to lower everyday costs, support fair wages and make child care affordable.
Wants to protect rural hospitals, lower medicine costs and expand behavioral health care.
Supports good schools and help for teachers across the district.
Seeks infrastructure investment for every parish plus workforce training and small-business support.
Pledges to stay accessible to constituents and work across party lines.
Authored a 2023 bill creating a Louisiana Community Health Worker Workforce Board.

economy.evidence: General statement: campaign pledges to support fair wages and lower everyday costs for working families.

welfare.evidence: Campaigns on affordable child care and lower health care costs, including for seniors.

liberty.evidence: Guns only: voted in 2024 against SB1, which allowed concealed carry of handguns without a permit; no clear record reviewed on other liberty issues.

security.evidence: Voted in 2024 against HB2, which gave police officers immunity from civil liability.

education.evidence: General statement: emphasizes good schools and support for teachers.

notes: Searched the campaign site, Wikipedia, legislative vote summaries and race coverage; her carbon capture votes were mixed, so energy is left blank. No statements found on immigration, foreign policy, tech or faith.

name: Austin Magee
current_role: Owner of an industrial welding and mechanical company
bio: Austin Magee owns Pittman Industrial, a welding and mechanical contracting company based in Washington Parish, and is from Franklinton. He attended Southeastern Louisiana University and has not previously sought public office. He took part in a spring 2026 Republican primary debate in Livingston Parish.

platform.point: Says he will resist government overreach that erodes individual freedoms.
Presents his work experience as a basis for practical, common-sense representation.
Cites a Bible verse, James 4:17, as his reason for running.
Runs as an outsider who says he never wanted a political career.

liberty.evidence: General statement: says government overreach eroding individual liberties worries him most; he names no specific issue.

faith.evidence: General statement: his campaign biography frames his candidacy as a religious duty, citing James 4:17.

notes: Searched the campaign site (home, about), local news and debate coverage; the Livingston Parish News debate report was blocked and other coverage gave no specific positions for him. Still unknown: his views on every topic except general statements on liberty and faith.

name: Oscar Dantzler
current_role: Former police officer and school bus driver
bio: Oscar "Omar" Dantzler is from Hammond and has a background in law enforcement, bail bonds and school bus driving in Tangipahoa Parish. He ran for the 5th District as a Democrat in 2022 and sought the governorship in 2019 and 2023. He qualified as a Republican for the 2026 race.
notes: Searched news coverage, iVoterGuide (he answered none of its 2022 questions) and Vote-USA (no issue responses); no campaign website or public issue statements were found. All ten topics remain unknown.

name: Dan McKay
bio: Dan McKay Jr. is a Bunkie attorney with about 45 years of practice, including more than 15 years as a public defender and more than 11 as an assistant district attorney. He is a U.S. Army Vietnam-era veteran who reached the rank of captain in the reserve. He grew up in Mangham in a cotton-farming family and is a past president of the Louisiana City Attorneys Association.

platform.point: Warns that Medicaid cuts threaten rural hospitals, including 17 in the 5th District.
Lists education, the economy, the environment and jobs as his main concerns.
Criticizes the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, calling it Trump's war.
Calls for moving past culture-war fights toward issues that help people economically.

welfare.evidence: Warns that Medicaid cuts will harm rural hospitals in the district, indicating opposition to those cuts.

foreign.evidence: General statement: criticizes the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, calling it Trump's war, without describing a broader foreign policy.

notes: Searched the campaign site (homepage only, no issues pages), the Hammond Star profile and KNOE coverage. He has named education, the environment and jobs as concerns without specifics, so most topics remain unknown.

name: Antonio Wilson
current_role: Licensed general contractor and business owner
bio: Antonio Wilson is a licensed general contractor and business owner from Tallulah whose work has included roads, water systems, housing and public facilities. His campaign presents a builder-style agenda of measurable projects and pledges to work with members of both parties. He joined the 5th District race in August 2026.

platform.point: Plans to recruit employers in manufacturing, logistics, agricultural processing, health care and technology.
Wants federal training dollars tied to hiring commitments from local employers.
Seeks wider access to capital and simpler federal programs for small businesses.
Pushes federal funding to keep rural hospitals open and to expand telemedicine.
Supports programs combining child care, education and job training, and more child care slots.
Calls for water and sewer upgrades, road and bridge repair, broadband, and flood protection in rural areas.
Proposes a public online dashboard tracking federal funding and project progress in the district.

economy.evidence: Campaign plans active federal involvement in recruiting employers and tying federal training funds to local hiring; this is a general agenda with no named bills.

welfare.evidence: General statement: supports federal funding for rural hospitals, telemedicine, senior services and expanded child care programs.

notes: Found and read his campaign site (home, about, FAQ and two commitment pages); an August 2026 Louisiana Illuminator report says he joined the race that month, though the article itself could not be opened. His site does not address social issues, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech or faith.

name: Chauna Banks
current_role: Former East Baton Rouge Metro Council member
bio: Chauna Banks represented District 2 on the East Baton Rouge Metro Council from 2013 through 2024. She spent more than two decades in public education and has worked in community and economic development. She holds a computer science degree from Southern University and campaigns under the slogan People Before Politics.

platform.point: Support small businesses, expand workforce training and attract well-paying jobs to the district.
Invest in schools, support teachers and build pathways to student success.
Protect and expand access to affordable, quality healthcare.
Lists infrastructure, transportation and disaster recovery support among her priorities.
Links public safety to the conditions in communities.
Campaigns on affordable housing and economic security for Louisiana families.
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Wants better access to capital and federal contracting for small businesses.

economy.evidence: General statement: says full-time workers should be able to afford housing and retirement, and backs affordable housing and small-business capital access.

welfare.evidence: Campaign pledges to protect and expand access to affordable healthcare and to protect Social Security and Medicare.

security.evidence: On the Metro Council she sponsored a $5 million settlement for Alton Sterling's family, citing police department hiring failures, and voted for the $4.5 million settlement in 2021.

education.evidence: Campaign calls for investing in schools and supporting teachers.

notes: Searched her campaign site, launch coverage and Metro Council news; her site repeats placeholder text under several priority headings, so those points rely on the launch coverage. No statements found on social issues, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech or faith.
